question:
A 30-year-old woman comes to the clinic with persistent low back pain that has lasted for 5 months.
The pain began after she slipped on ice outside her home and has not resolved. Radiologic imaging
shows no fractures. She reports using ice and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, which provide
temporary moderate relief, but the pain quickly returns. She localizes the pain to the bilateral paraspinal
muscles in the lower lumbar region. On physical examination, which of the following findings is most
likely to be observed? Answer Choices: (A) Spastic paravertebral lumbar musculature (B) Positive
straight leg raise test bilaterally (C) Decreased lumbar lordosis with muscle guarding (D) Asymmetric
paraspinal muscle tone (E) Trigger points in the quadratus lumborum (F) Boggy soft tissues in the
lumbar region (G) Visible muscle atrophy in the lumbar region (H) Hyperpigmentation of the overlying
skin (I) Point tenderness over L4-L5 spinous processes (J) Dry, scaly, itchy skin over the lumbar
musculature
 A. Trigger points in the quadratus lumborum
B. Spastic paravertebral lumbar musculature
C. Asymmetric paraspinal muscle tone

D. Boggy soft tissues in the lumbar region
E. Hyperpigmentation of the overlying skin
F. Decreased lumbar lordosis with muscle guarding
G. Point tenderness over L4-L5 spinous processes
H. Dry, scaly, itchy skin over the lumbar musculature
I. Visible muscle atrophy in the lumbar region
J. Positive straight leg raise test bilaterally
